proposal.brain.ml.a-calculation-cannot-d.for: the whole point of declaring produces and consumes is that a program is refused before it runs, not during it
proposal.brain.ml.a-calculation-cannot-d.proposal: an optional args schema on Calculation (names and whether required) checked by PCR.calc at author time, the way a read of a later sibling's Part already is
proposal.brain.ml.a-calculation-cannot-d.text: a Calculation is a pure function of one mapping, and nothing at author time says which keys it needs. a missing args['seed'] or args['target'] surfaces as a KeyError deep inside a Tick, after the run has started and after earlier Ticks have already written their Parts.
proposal.brain.ml.a-calculation-cannot-d.workaround: each calculation reads its required keys first and raises a named error; the tests assert the refusal

proposal.brain.ml.a-clustering-fixture-c.for: a test that fails for its fixture teaches the reader to loosen the assertion, which is how a real regression gets through
proposal.brain.ml.a-clustering-fixture-c.proposal: harness.synthetic should take the structure it is drawing (blobs, classes, a low-rank matrix) and guarantee the property the caller is about to test for, rather than returning a draw and leaving the property to luck
proposal.brain.ml.a-clustering-fixture-c.text: synthetic_blobs drew k centres from one normal and hoped: at several seeds two centres landed closer than a standard deviation, and k-means was blamed for not separating blobs that were never separate. the same trap is waiting in every seeded fixture that draws a structure and then tests for it.
proposal.brain.ml.a-clustering-fixture-c.workaround: the generator now redraws centres from the same seeded stream until their minimum pairwise distance clears a multiple of the spread, and scales them apart if it cannot

proposal.brain.ml.a-fitted-model-is-a-pa.for: an ml layer whose models only exist inside a process cannot be audited, compared or replayed
proposal.brain.ml.a-fitted-model-is-a-pa.text: fit and predict are separate Calculations and the model between them is a json-able dict at px.exp.brain.result.ml.<model>.<case>. the receipt digests it, PQL finds it, and predicting from a model a different run fitted costs nothing.

proposal.brain.ml.a-linear-speed-criteri.for: a tournament whose verdict is an artefact of its normalisation teaches the wrong lesson and is worse than no tournament
proposal.brain.ml.a-linear-speed-criteri.proposal: harness.decide should offer a log or a rank normalisation per criterion, declared in the criterion next to its direction and weight, so timing criteria are not silently linear
proposal.brain.ml.a-linear-speed-criteri.text: scored on raw milliseconds, the bracket's winner flipped: min-max normalising wall time across candidates lets one slow branch compress the fast ones into a rounding difference, and a docstring then decided a 22x speed gap.
proposal.brain.ml.a-linear-speed-criteri.workaround: the criterion recorded in the bracket is log2 of the median, so a constant factor is a constant distance whatever the spread of the field

proposal.brain.ml.a-record-inlines-value.for: records are supposed to make a run replayable and auditable; at this rate the record of a real dataset is unreadable and unreviewable, and a landing diff is dominated by it
proposal.brain.ml.a-record-inlines-value.proposal: run_record should write a reference (address plus produce_sha256) instead of the value whenever the value is published to a Part in the same store, with the full rendering kept for values that are not
proposal.brain.ml.a-record-inlines-value.text: run_record renders every produced value into the record, so a 300-row dataset Part is written twice: once in store/ml.json and again, in full, inside records/ml.classification.json. this vertical's records are 200kb each and the duplication is all of it. the address and the digest are already in the record; the value is not new information.
proposal.brain.ml.a-record-inlines-value.workaround: the datasets a bracket only needs as input are stored as a recipe Part (the calculation and its args) rather than as rows, so the record carries the seed instead of the draw

proposal.brain.ml.a-run-record-cannot-be.for: the contract asks for a record of every PCR run in every landing; a record that cannot be committed cleanly is not a record anyone keeps
proposal.brain.ml.a-run-record-cannot-be.proposal: run_record should take timings='measured'|'blank' (or write them to a sibling file), so the durable half of a record and the unrepeatable half are not the same bytes
proposal.brain.ml.a-run-record-cannot-be.text: pyto.materialize.run_record puts wall-clock readings (counters.wall_ms, each invocation's duration_ms) into the record, so the file's bytes change on every run. committed, it conflicts between any two branches that both re-ran the program, and any suite that regenerates it leaves the tree dirty behind a landing. it cost this vertical three refused landings and two other verticals one each.
proposal.brain.ml.a-run-record-cannot-be.workaround: parts.settle() blanks every *_ms key before write_record, so the file is a function of the run and not of the stopwatch; the timings that are a claim live in benchmark Parts, which say how many samples they are the median of

proposal.brain.ml.an-approximate-backend.for: the contract's rule is that a backend which changes semantics is a failed backend; an approximation is a different calculation, and saying so in the oracle is what keeps the rule enforceable
proposal.brain.ml.an-approximate-backend.text: the histogram split search is not the sorting one to 1e-9 and never will be: it scans bin edges, not midpoints. its oracle is not equality but the held-out accuracy of the exact tree within a stated margin, recorded in the same oracle Part shape as every exact one.

proposal.brain.ml.newton-beats-descent-o.for: gradient descent is the default in most teaching code; on this shape it is the slowest correct answer, and the bracket is the evidence rather than the opinion
proposal.brain.ml.newton-beats-descent-o.text: the logistic bracket says it plainly: on 400 rows and 6 columns, newton/irls through numpy is about 22 times faster than the same steps in python and about 200 times faster than full-batch gradient descent, and all three land on scipy's penalised optimum. the cost of newton is a solve per step, and one weighted matmul pays for it.

proposal.brain.ml.one-address-scheme-mad.for: the brief asks for the territory as Parts readable through PQL; the address scheme is why that cost nothing to produce and nothing to keep true
proposal.brain.ml.one-address-scheme-mad.text: because every part is at px.exp.brain.<kind>.<vertical>.<name>, the map Part's built list is literally the store's own address list, and the shared map module counts kinds and verticals with prefix queries and nothing else. no vertical had to register anything or tell anyone what it had made.

proposal.brain.ml.one-pairwise-distance-.for: it is the single hottest kernel in the unsupervised half, and three copies means three places for a backend to change semantics
proposal.brain.ml.one-pairwise-distance-.proposal: fn.brain.backend.pairwise(metric) as one calculation in the backend vertical, with knn, silhouette, k-means and dbscan routed through it and one oracle against scipy.spatial.distance.cdist covering all four
proposal.brain.ml.one-pairwise-distance-.text: knn_predict, silhouette and (next) k-means each build the same n-by-n euclidean matrix, each with their own np spelling of it. the identity |a-b|^2 = |a|^2 - 2ab + |b|^2 is written twice already in this vertical.
proposal.brain.ml.one-pairwise-distance-.workaround: knn_predict uses the matmul identity, silhouette uses the broadcast subtraction; both are oracled against scipy cdist so at least they agree

proposal.brain.ml.pql-cannot-select-on-a.for: the brief says use PQL to navigate what you are building; a query you cannot store is not navigation, it is a script
proposal.brain.ml.pql-cannot-select-on-a.proposal: PQL.field('pass', False) / PQL.field('backend', 'np') composing with prefix and where, so a query stays a value and can itself be a Part
proposal.brain.ml.pql-cannot-select-on-a.text: navigating this store means questions like 'every oracle that failed' or 'every benchmark of the np backend'. PQL.prefix gets to the subtree, but the selection itself is a python closure over match.value written at each call site, so the query is not a value that can be stored, named or put in a record.
proposal.brain.ml.pql-cannot-select-on-a.workaround: parts.navigate() holds the handful of closures the vertical actually asks and returns their answers as plain data

proposal.brain.ml.pxc-has-no-document.for: the store is where the night's work lives; persisting it is not a per-vertical concern
proposal.brain.ml.pxc-has-no-document.proposal: PxC.document(exclude_prefix='px.receipt.') and PxC.merge(document), so a store round-trips through json in the kernel and every vertical's persistence is the same code
proposal.brain.ml.pxc-has-no-document.text: PxC can be walked (addresses, PQL.prefix) but cannot hand back or take in a whole document, so every vertical writes its own save/load pair and its own receipt-exclusion rule.
proposal.brain.ml.pxc-has-no-document.workaround: Store.document()/save()/load_store() in experiments/brain/ml/parts.py, written to the shape the shared harness will expose

proposal.brain.ml.seed-in-args-makes-one.for: the contract's rule that a backend which changes semantics is a failed backend is only checkable if the randomness is shared
proposal.brain.ml.seed-in-args-makes-one.text: every seeded calculation here reads one deterministic Stream built from args['seed'], never random or numpy's generator. the py and np backends then return the same bytes, so a seeded calculation needs one oracle instead of one per backend, and a record replays exactly.

proposal.brain.ml.seeded-init-is-what-ma.for: clustering is the family where nobody can tell a faster implementation from a luckier one, unless the seed is an argument
proposal.brain.ml.seeded-init-is-what-ma.text: all three k-means branches read one Stream built from args['seed'] for the k-means++ init, so py, np and the gram-matrix branch start from the same centres and their oracle is exact equality of labels and inertia. without that the bracket would be comparing dice.

proposal.brain.ml.the-bracket-refuses-to.for: the one failure mode of a tournament is choosing the criteria after seeing the numbers; a rule that is enforced by the store is worth more than a rule in a contract
proposal.brain.ml.the-bracket-refuses-to.text: harness.bracket refuses a bracket with no criteria, harness.judge refuses a score for a criterion the bracket did not record and refuses a judge whose name is one of the candidate branches, and harness.decide refuses to decide while any candidate is unjudged. writing the criteria first stopped being a discipline and became a thing the code will not let you skip.

proposal.brain.ml.worker-sessions-could-.for: a tournament judged by the same agent that built the candidates is weaker evidence, and the surface built in a night is bounded by how much one session can write
proposal.brain.ml.worker-sessions-could-.proposal: the sprint harness should hand each vertical a way to run a scoped worker session, or the contract should say plainly that a recorded, re-runnable scoring function is the judge of record
proposal.brain.ml.worker-sessions-could-.text: the vertical was briefed to fan out to parallel worker sessions for each build and each tournament judge. every route to one was refused in this environment, so the whole vertical was built serially in one session and the tournament judges are deterministic scoring functions over the recorded criteria instead of separate readers.
proposal.brain.ml.worker-sessions-could-.workaround: criteria are written into the bracket Part before any score exists, the judge is a pure function of the oracle and benchmark Parts, and a test re-runs the whole bracket from the candidates so the verdict is reproducible rather than trusted

stubbed.why: boosting here is squared loss only; the logistic loss needs a second-order step and its own oracle
the out-of-bag rows are recorded per tree (oob_sizes) but nothing scores on them yet
the backward pass is hand-derived for exactly one hidden layer; a second layer needs autograd or another hand derivation, and a half-checked one is worth less than none
one alpha is fitted and oracled; the path over a grid of alphas is a loop away and is the part worth reading
kfold and every metric exist; the loop that folds them together is still at each call site
multiclass is one-vs-rest, not a softmax; the softmax needs its own oracle and is not worth a half-checked one
the exact vote is the reference; a kd-tree or ball-tree is a backend of it, and belongs after the shared pairwise-distance primitive
